Alex: quick update — ran a focused RoPE head/kv-scale sweep across llama-2-13b and mistral-7b (NTK vs linear vs YARN variants). saw a reproducible perplexity cliff + latency cliff on mistral longctx when head_scale ~1.25-1.35. dashboard: https://internal.redwood/d/rope-headscale-sweep :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Sam: ok can you drop the profile/snippet?
Alex: copying the perf snippet we captured on the slow step (kernel switch + cache miss):
```
p99=312ms p50=42ms tokens=2048 model=mistral-7b variant=ntk head_scale=1.3 kernel=matmul_opt fallback=matmul_generic
CPU% kernel_selector=0.12 batching_wait=8ms kv_cache_evictions=3 prefix_cache_hits=12
backtrace: kernel_selector -> choose_kernel_v2 -> fallback_path
```
Priya: interesting — kv_cache_evictions jumping is the red flag. @Cheng any thoughts on cache alignment with larger head scales?
Cheng: head_scale stretches the rotary phase offsets; on some kernels we end up with inefficient head-splitting that prevents contiguous KV tile reuse. that plus a rare cache alignment mismatch triggers eviction heuristics.
Marisol: any signs this is model-specific (llama vs mistral) or kernel-implementation specific?
Alex: appears both. llama-2-13b tolerated head_scale up to 1.5 without perplexity bump, but mixtral/mistral showed quality regression earlier. kernel logs show different kernel selection thresholds across devices.
Sam: can we reproduce with a synthetic microbench to isolate kernel selector? maybe run: 
```bash
python tools/bench/kernel_selector_sweep.py --model mistral-7b --variant ntk --head-scale 1.0 1.1 1.2 1.3 1.4 --seq-len 4096
```
Priya: +1, also add --kv-alignment-debug to bench script so we can print tile offsets.
perf-bot: [profile-uploaded] file=rope_headscale_mistral_ntk_1.3.pbz size=4.2MB link=https://internal.redwood/artifacts/rope_headscale_mistral_ntk_1.3
Cheng: probable mitigation paths: 1) tighten kernel selection threshold so we avoid fallback at borderline perf; 2) add an alignment-aware eviction cooldown so a few transient misalignments don't evict; 3) consider a head-scale-aware KV packing strategy for Mistral kernels.
Marisol: operational question — are customers likely to hit this in prod? which routes + sequence length?
Alex: saw this in longctx routes (>=4096) with mixed prefix lengths common in chat-history workloads. only in Dedicated on newer kernels so far.
Sam: can we create a small canary: change selector in staging to be more conservative, run 24h repeating gen load across seq lens 1024/2048/4096 and watch p95/p99?
Alex: will set up canary job tonight and post results tomorrow morning.
Priya: also add a prompt set to the eval harness to guard quality (perplexity + BERT score) so we detect regressions automatically.
Cheng: I'll draft a kernel-change PR with selector threshold and a micro-optim to avoid head-split when head_scale > 1.2.
Marisol: thanks — please @channel the canary link when up. :thumbsup:
Alex: noted, will share artifacts and a short triage doc after the first canary run.
